items.title: Vietnamese business outlet CafeF reports Gucci facing public backlash over $1,000 'Made in China' Drip sneaker
items.summary: CafeF, a major Vietnamese business/finance portal, covers the Drip sneaker controversy for Vietnamese readers, framing it as Gucci 'hung bua riu du luan' (facing a wave of public criticism) for abandoning its Italian manufacturing pride while keeping the roughly $1,000 price tag unchanged. Cites Gucci's revenue collapse from EUR10.49bn (2022) to EUR7.7bn (2024) and consultant framing that 'Made in China is not a good look' for a luxury house. Confirms the manufacturing-provenance story reached Vietnamese-language business audiences directly.

items.title: Inside Retail Asia analyzes why Gucci's 'Made in China' Drip sneaker is raising questions for the brand's price-value equation
items.summary: Asia-Pacific retail trade outlet examines the Drip sneaker (EUR800/US$1,000, designed by Demna) as the first Gucci footwear explicitly labelled Made in China, while every other shoe on Gucci's site remains Italian-made. Quotes Gucci's own statement that 'Italy would always be at the heart of Gucci's manufacturing model' alongside analyst warnings that Chinese-made product could 'fuel debate around the brand's price value equation.' Notes Gucci sales have halved over three years and Kering has cut prices on select products, situating the story within broader APAC retail-industry concern.

items.title: Malaysian business outlet BusinessToday covers Gucci's break from Italian sneaker-manufacturing tradition with the Drip
items.summary: BusinessToday Malaysia reports on the Drip, Demna's debut sneaker for Gucci, noting its laceless sock-like silhouette, nylon/canvas/suede options, and the Made in China label breaking with a 100-year Italian-manufacturing identity, framed for Malaysian business readers amid Gucci's ongoing sales slump. Confirms the controversy reached a fourth distinct SEA national market (after Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam) this cycle.

items.title: Tatler Asia covers Gucci's renovated flagship reopening, part of regional store-network refresh coverage
items.summary: Tatler Asia, the region's top T2 luxury-lifestyle title, runs renovation/reopening coverage of a Gucci flagship (Art Deco-inspired redesign with rosewood, marble, and a private VIP lounge), part of the brand's broader store-network refresh storyline that Tatler has tracked across Asian flagships this year, including Singapore's Marina Bay Sands location. Positive activation-style coverage, discounted per sentiment-rubric treatment of brand-owned store news.

items.title: VnExpress International reports Vietnam crackdown busts warehouses full of counterfeit Gucci, Dior, Hermes goods
items.summary: Vietnam's leading English-language outlet reports police raids on warehouses storing counterfeit Gucci, Dior and Hermes goods, part of an intensifying national crackdown on fake luxury goods. While not a Gucci-authored story, it signals the scale of counterfeit demand/supply tied to the Gucci name in the Vietnamese market and the reputational exposure of unauthorized goods trading on brand equity.

items.title: Thai entertainment media account posts about Gucci brand ambassador Song Weilong at Gucci Central Embassy Bangkok store event
items.summary: Thai pop-culture X account Mint Magazine Thailand posted photos of Chinese actor and Gucci brand ambassador Song Weilong at the Gucci Central Embassy Bangkok store celebration, part of recurring ambassador-driven activation content aimed at Thai fan communities. Included only as context for SEA ambassador-marketing volume; this specific post is outside the 14-day freshness window (dated January 2026) and is NOT counted toward today's buzz scoring -- flagged here rather than silently dropped so the gap in fresh SNS supply is visible.

coverage_notes: SEA pool for 2026-10-03 is news-dominated: 5 admitted news items (T2 regional/trade press across Vietnam, Malaysia, and pan-APAC) anchored on the 'Made in China' Drip sneaker critical-angle story, plus one Tatler Asia flagship-reopening activation item. Critical-angle searches (price hike, quality complaints, resale drop, boycott, overrated, counterfeit) were run in English, Thai, Bahasa Indonesia, and Vietnamese; they surfaced the sneaker-manufacturing backlash (dominant critical story this week, see SEA-2026-10-03-01/02/03) and a Vietnam counterfeit-warehouse bust, but turned up no SEA-specific resale-price-drop or boycott content and no fresh (within 14 days) verifiable SNS/community posts with visible engagement metrics. A Thai X/ambassador post was found but is dated January 2026 (outside the freshness window) and is logged only as context, excluded from scoring -- genuine shortfall, not padded. Pantip (Thailand) and Kaskus (Indonesia) community threads on Gucci exist but carry no visible publish dates or engagement counts within the search results, so none were admitted this cycle.
